grammar.label: evaluative that-clauses — the fact that, the problem is that
grammar.form: the fact / problem / difficulty / point / trouble + that-clause
grammar.meaning: names what kind of thing the following clause is

explanation.en: 'The difficulty is that nobody kept a record.' The noun does the evaluating before the clause has even been read: 'the fact that' presents as settled, 'the claim that' as contested, 'the trouble with that is' as fatal. 'The fact that' is the most abused: writers use it to smuggle a contested claim past the reader as established.
explanation.uz: 'The difficulty is that nobody kept a record.' Ot baho beradi: 'the fact that' — hal qilingan, 'the claim that' — bahsli. 'The fact that' eng ko'p suiiste'mol qilinadi.

grammar.positive_example: The claim that the road was never finished rests on a single letter.
grammar.negative_example: The fact that the road was never finished rests on a single letter.

l1_notes.uz: Bu qurilma o'zbek tilida '-ligi' qo'shimchasi bilan beriladi va baho ohangi yo'qoladi.

grammar.label: graduation — turning the volume of a description up or down
grammar.form: somewhat / fairly / rather / decidedly / distinctly / markedly + adjective; a shade / a good deal + comparative
grammar.meaning: moves a description along a scale without changing the word

explanation.en: English grades with adverbs rather than with endings. 'Rather good' is warmer than 'fairly good' and cooler than 'decidedly good'; 'a shade too long' is gentler than 'far too long'. British English uses understatement here in a way that misleads learners — 'not entirely successful' can mean a failure, and 'rather disappointing' can be severe.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tili bahoni qo'shimcha bilan emas, ravish bilan o'lchaydi. Britan ingliz tilida kamaytirib aytish ko'p: 'not entirely successful' aslida muvaffaqiyatsizlikni bildirishi mumkin.

grammar.positive_example: The second draft is a good deal clearer, though still rather long.
grammar.negative_example: The second draft is very more clear, though still very long.

l1_notes.uz: Kamaytirib aytish o'zbek va rus madaniyatida kamroq; 'rather disappointing' ni yumshoq tanqid deb tushunish xato.

body.text: 'The fact that' says it is settled. Is it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: One letter, and nobody has checked it.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then 'the claim that'. You have just smuggled a contested thing past your reader as established, and I doubt you meant to.
